metadata.title: Plan and Design Template
metadata.purposeAndUsage: Analyze requirements and design a new process template. Use before creating template files.

output.description: Complete template design including purpose, parameters, steps, and flow diagram

prerequisites: Clear understanding of the workflow to be templated
Knowledge of existing templates and steps
specificActions: Follow the substeps below in sequence
Workflow: review requirements → check existing → purpose → use cases → check reusable steps → plan steps → identify parameters → design flow → create diagram
Before planning steps: Check existing generic steps in .processes/steps/planning/ and .processes/steps/common/
When planning steps: Prefer reusable step categories
When planning steps: Ensure each step represents actual work, not flow control
Use camelCase for parameter names: featureName, targetBranch

update: memory.json (current step section with design details)

tools: read_file - Read existing templates and steps
list_dir - Explore existing templates and step categories
bestPractices: Check existing templates before creating new ones

STEP REUSE FIRST: Before proposing ANY new step, explicitly search existing steps (planning/, common/, investigation/, learning/) to see if they can handle the use case with different parameters or scope. Only propose a new step after confirming no existing step can be adapted.
Keep templates focused on a single workflow
Always include continuous improvement as final step with approvalRequired: true
Use clear parameter naming with camelCase
Design steps to produce tangible outputs
Ensure flow diagram matches step sequence
Consider guideline-based steps for team flexibility (see guidelineBasedStepPattern)
Embed Q&A within steps, not as standalone steps - use qa-session component (see qaAsSubstepPattern)
Design feedback loops for iterative processes - allow returning to gather more info (see feedbackLoopsPattern)

guidelineBasedStepPattern.description: Use guideline-based steps when teams need flexibility in how they perform a step
whenToUse: Data collection varies by team (e.g., Jira vs docs vs interviews)
Teams have different tools or formats (e.g., diagram types, LLD formats)
Methods differ across organizations (e.g., testing approaches, review processes)
Step requires domain-specific knowledge that varies
howToImplement: Mark the step as guideline-based in the template
Step JSON references a guideline file that teams customize
Provide sensible defaults in the step itself
examples: Get parameters from external systems (Jira, Azure DevOps, docs)
Create design documents (different formats per team)

qaAsSubstepPattern.description: Embed Q&A within steps rather than creating standalone Q&A steps
qaAsSubstepPattern.rationale: Q&A naturally occurs during multiple steps - a standalone Q&A step is artificial and creates unnecessary process overhead
whenToUse: Information gaps are discovered during step execution
User clarification is needed before proceeding
howToImplement: Do NOT create a standalone Q&A step in the template
Instead, add Q&A as a substep within relevant steps
Steps that commonly need Q&A: context understanding, information gathering, design creation

substeps.name: Q&A Session (if needed)
substeps.description: Use qa-session component to gather missing information

qaAsSubstepPattern.antiPattern: Creating a dedicated 'Q&A Step' or 'Answer Open Questions' step in the template flow

feedbackLoopsPattern.description: Design process flows that can loop back to earlier steps when additional information or work is needed
feedbackLoopsPattern.rationale: During analysis or creation phases, gaps are often discovered that require returning to information gathering. Rigid linear flows force workarounds or incomplete work.
whenToUse: Analysis steps may reveal missing information
Creation/design steps may need additional context
Validation steps may require corrections in earlier outputs
howToImplement: Identify steps that commonly discover information gaps (analysis, design, creation)
Add conditional return paths to information gathering steps
In mermaid diagram: add decision diamonds with 'Need more info?' branches
Document the feedback loop trigger conditions in step descriptions
feedbackLoopsPattern.mermaidExample:
graph TD
    A[Gather Info] --> B[Analyze]
    B --> C{Info Complete?}
    C -->|No| A
    C -->|Yes| D[Create Design]
    D --> E{Gaps Found?}
    E -->|Yes| A
    E -->|No| F[Done]
feedbackLoopsPattern.antiPattern: Forcing strictly linear flows where steps cannot revisit earlier work when needed

substeps.name: Init-Step: Confirm Principles
substeps.description: Recall operating principles before starting this step
actions: Read `.processes/steps/_components/operating-principles.md` and recall all principles
Output: '✓ Principles confirmed for this step'

substeps.name: Review requirements
substeps.description: Understand what workflow needs to be templated
actions: Review the stated need for a new template
Identify the workflow to be standardized
Document expected outcomes

substeps.name: Check existing templates
substeps.description: Verify no similar template already exists
actions: List existing templates
Search for similar workflows
Identify templates that could be extended vs creating new

substeps.name: Write purpose statement
substeps.description: Define clear purpose for the template
actions: Write one-sentence purpose statement
Describe what workflow the template enables
Ensure purpose is specific and actionable

substeps.name: Define use cases
substeps.description: Document when to use this template
actions: List scenarios where template applies
Define prerequisites or conditions
Identify target users

substeps.name: Check existing reusable steps
substeps.description: Identify steps that can be reused
actions: Review .processes/steps/planning/ for planning steps
Review .processes/steps/common/ for utility steps
Review .processes/steps/investigation/ for analysis steps
List existing steps that fit the workflow

substeps.name: Plan step breakdown
actions: Break workflow into logical stages
FOR EACH STAGE: First search existing steps that could handle the requirement with different parameters/scope before proposing a new step
Assign steps to each stage (strongly prefer reusing existing steps)
Define expected output for each step
Ensure each step produces tangible work
Identify which steps need user approval before proceeding (mark with approvalRequired: true)
For each step, ask: 'Would teams benefit from flexibility here?' If yes, consider guideline-based approach (see guidelineBasedStepPattern)

substeps.name: Identify parameters
actions: Identify values that must be provided by user (required)
Identify values that are helpful but optional
Use camelCase naming
Document parameter purposes

substeps.name: Design process flow
substeps.description: Map out the logical flow of the template
actions: Design sequential flow of steps
Identify decision points and branches
Plan sync points if sub-processes involved
Consider feedback loops: Can analysis/creation steps return to gather more info? (see feedbackLoopsPattern)

substeps.name: Create mermaid diagram
actions: Create mermaid flowchart syntax
Include all steps and decision points
Ensure diagram matches planned steps
Document design in memory

substeps.name: End-Step: Compliance Check
substeps.description: Verify principles were followed in this step
actions: Verify: Was log.json updated for any user interactions?
Verify: Were mandatory actions confirmed with output?
Verify: Do modified process files conform to type definitions? (Principle 7 - see `.processes/steps/_components/operating-principles.md`)
Output: '✓ Step completed in compliance with operating principles'

flow.description: Linear flow through all 9 substeps: requirements → existing check → purpose → use cases → reusable steps → step breakdown → parameters → flow design → diagram

fields: Information Produced: Purpose statement, parameters list, step breakdown, flow diagram
Decisions Made: Step organization, parameter choices, reusable step selections
